clue.text: Be clearly out when turning ball goes to fielder

parts.note: in cricket a break is a ball that turns sharply off the pitch
cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side, so the fielder there is called cover

explanation.surface: A batsman is plainly out when a spinning delivery is caught by a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'out' look like a dismissal, but the definition means emerging into the open, as hunted game does.
explanation.definitionFit: To break cover is to leave a hiding place and come out openly into view, as an animal does.

clue.text: Space to tie a ship up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: to moor a ship is to tie it up at a berth

explanation.surface: Instructions on finding enough room to secure a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Room and space are synonyms for an area that is free to be occupied.

clue.text: A quiet look by doctor showing confidence

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor's calm, silent glance conveys assurance to a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and composure, a near synonym of confidence.

clue.text: Show concern about horse slaughter

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to care is to show concern
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Someone shows worry about a horse being slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is large-scale killing, the same as slaughter on a battlefield.

clue.text: Big star gave trouble

indicators.note: trouble is read as a verb meaning to disturb, so the letters of the word before it are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity caused problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big star' suggests a celebrity behaving badly, but it means an actual star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Red rose embroidered for church screen

indicators.note: embroidered suggests the words are worked over and rearranged like threads in needlework

explanation.surface: A red rose is stitched onto a church screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind a church altar.

clue.text: A way to regulate the economy from Roman times

definitions.text: A way to regulate the economy

indicators.note: from means the answer is derived or made out of the following letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: An economic policy dating back to the Roman era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the answer is built out of the letters of ROMAN TIMES, rearranged; the surface reads it as an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetarism is the economic doctrine of controlling the money supply to manage inflation.

clue.text: House calls may double a salesman's objective

indicators.note: may double means the word supplied is written twice in succession

parts.note: a salesman aims to secure an order from a customer

explanation.surface: Doctors' visits might double what a sales rep is after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House calls' looks like doctors' home visits; it is the Speaker of the House of Commons calling the chamber to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker in the UK House of Commons calls out this repeated cry to restore quiet in debate.

clue.text: Be mother for the French

definitions.meaning: to be mother is the British idiom for serving the tea, filling everyone's cups
the French word for 'for' is spelt this way

explanation.definitionFit: Being mother means serving tea from the pot, and French uses this word to mean for.

clue.text: Jovial acknowledgement of a bad standard

parts.note: jolly means jovial and cheerful
roger is the radio word acknowledging a message received

explanation.surface: A cheerful reply about low standards.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones pirate flag is a standard, or banner, flown by villains.

clue.text: Spent two notes at the charity 'do'

parts.note: E and F are two notes of the musical scale
a fete is an outdoor fundraising event, often for charity

explanation.surface: Someone paid out on two banknotes at a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like paying money, and 'notes' like banknotes, but the definition means exhausted and the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete can mean worn out and lacking vigour, as something spent is exhausted.

clue.text: Unusually big task carried out by servicemen

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Soldiers complete an extraordinarily large job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'carried out' as completing a task; the definition is the bags soldiers carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitbags are long canvas bags in which soldiers and sailors carry their equipment.

clue.text: Fouled player retaliated

definitions.meaning: a footballer who kicked a defender, or back, fouled that player
to kick back is to hit back at someone in retaliation

explanation.definitionFit: Kicking back means striking in return, and literally kicking a defender is a foul.

clue.text: Watch recording of US welcome for celebrity

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch, from its ticking
tape is a recording medium, and a recording itself

explanation.surface: Viewing footage of an American reception for a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: American cities hold parades showering paper streamers on returning heroes and celebrities.

clue.text: Stuffed with chopped dates

indicators.note: chopped suggests the word is cut up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish filled with diced dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Sated means having eaten one's fill, so stuffed after a meal.

clue.text: She is used to having high scores

definitions.text: She is used to having high scores

parts.words: She is used to having high scores
parts.note: reads like a top player or gamer, but describes a female singer whose musical parts are written in the top range

explanation.definitionFit: This is the highest female singing voice, whose musical scores lie in the upper register.

clue.text: Strains to understand footnote

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone struggles hard to make sense of a note at the bottom of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' looks like effort, but is a verb meaning filters or oozes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that strains through a cloth oozes slowly through it, as it seeps.

clue.text: Sees a new way, relaxes

indicators.note: a new way means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fresh approach and calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or relax, as one eases off the pressure.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot a bird

definitions.meaning: to raise its hammer ready to fire
a male chicken or other male bird

explanation.definitionFit: Cocking a gun readies it to fire, and the word also means a male fowl.

clue.text: Prison for a highflier?

definitions.meaning: doing ... is British slang for serving time in prison
something that flies high in the sky, a feathered creature

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a prison sentence, and a winged creature that soars aloft.

clue.text: Gathers in spare parts

indicators.note: parts is read as a verb, so the word is parted and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collects spare components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare parts' reads as one phrase, but 'parts' is the signal and 'spare' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to harvest, gathering in a crop.

clue.text: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps

definitions.text: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps

parts.words: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps
parts.note: reads as reforming a political party; read as re- plus a word for a party or band, it means to form a group again

explanation.definitionFit: To reorganise or reassemble a body, as a defeated party may rebuild itself.

clue.text: Odd way to go from place to place

parts.note: St, street, is a way

parts.words: to go from place to place
parts.note: to range is to wander or roam over an area

explanation.surface: A peculiar method of travelling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and odd are synonyms meaning unusual.

clue.text: Chaps caught in foul deed are corrected

indicators.note: caught in means the chaps are trapped inside the other piece
foul means the letters of the next word are fouled up, or jumbled

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men involved in a wicked act are punished and set right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' jumbles the deed's letters to EDED; 'are' is a link, so the definition is the past participle alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing errors.

clue.text: Not a galley, but may be found in one

definitions.text: Not a galley, but may be found in one

parts.words: Not a galley, but may be found in one
parts.note: first read as a powered ship rather than an oared galley, then as a cooking pot in a ship's kitchen

explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered ship differs from an oared galley, and a steaming pan is used in a ship's kitchen.

clue.text: In the end mountain range finishes where Tunisia starts

parts.note: the Atlas is a mountain range in North Africa

indicators.note: starts means just the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A North African mountain range ends where Tunisia begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The geography is real: the Atlas range runs across to Tunisia, making the surface accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, after a long wait, so in the end.

clue.text: Non-bowler put into bowl

definitions.meaning: in cricket the player facing the bowler is the batsman
a mixture of flour, egg and milk poured into a mixing bowl

explanation.definitionFit: A player who bats rather than bowls, and the pancake mixture whisked in a bowl.

clue.text: On which landlubbers constitutionally walk the plank

definitions.text: On which landlubbers constitutionally walk the plank

parts.words: On which landlubbers constitutionally walk the plank
parts.note: suggests pirates' victims, but describes people taking a constitutional stroll along a planked seaside structure

explanation.definitionFit: A seaside walkway built on stilts over the water, with planked decking for strollers.

clue.text: Plead a case for right Austrian composer

indicators.note: a case for means the first piece forms a case around the second

parts.note: to beg is to plead

explanation.surface: A lawyer argues for an Austrian composer's rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Aligns East with East correctly

parts.note: the Orient is the East

indicators.note: correctly suggests the letters of the second word must be put right, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lining up one eastern direction with another properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate something is to align or position it in relation to compass points.

clue.text: Not the original journalist's work

definitions.meaning: a reproduction or duplicate rather than the original
the text a journalist writes for publication

explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate is not the original, and journalists' written material is called this.

clue.text: Part of centre-page spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A section of a newspaper's middle double-page layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-page spread' reads as a newspaper term; 'spread' is really the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a part or proportion of a whole.
